title: Emit zero or more results per element with mapMulti

blocks.text: `mapMulti` (Java 16) is a one-to-many mapping like `flatMap`, but instead of returning a stream per element it hands you a downstream consumer: call `downstream.accept(x)` once for each result you want to emit, as many times as you like, including not at all. Give it a type witness, `.<Integer>mapMulti(...)`, so the result type is known.
Write two methods in `Expand`; `mapMulti` fits both:

items: `valueAndSquare(List<Integer> numbers)` emits each number followed by its square.

`upperStrings(List<Object> mixed)` emits each element that is a `String` (even an empty one), upper-cased with `Locale.ROOT`, and nothing for any other element, other `CharSequence` types such as `StringBuilder` included.

blocks.text: A mixed list can hold anything, `null` included.

cases.says: Each number is followed by its square, and each string comes out upper-cased.
Elements that are not String emit nothing, other CharSequence types such as StringBuilder included.
A null element emits nothing instead of throwing NullPointerException; instanceof is false for null.
Upper-casing uses Locale.ROOT, so "this" becomes "THIS" even when the default locale is Turkish.

concepts: Emitting zero or more results per element keeps only the elements that qualify, skipping nulls and other types.
